note.note:
Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  1 week of sore throat followed by dry, non-productive cough; exertional shortness of breath for 3–4 days; mild wheeze; intermittent chest discomfort; initial fever for ~3 days now resolved; intermittent headaches; decreased appetite without reported weight loss. No known chronic medical conditions reported. No history of asthma or venous thromboembolism.
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Mother with lung cancer. No family history of clots reported.
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  No regular medications. Paracetamol recommended for symptom relief (dose/route/frequency not documented). Allergies noted: peanuts.
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded.
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  Not recorded.
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  Non-smoker; reports experimenting with smoking once or twice in the past. No known asbestos exposure. Performs exercise “now and then.” Recent decreased appetite; usual diet details not recorded. Alcohol and other substance use not recorded.
- Hearing and vision concerns:  Not recorded.
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):  Not recorded.
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:  Employed; requested sick note for time off work. Lives in the UK; born in the US; recent travel only within Europe. Safe and confidential place for consult confirmed. Other social determinants not recorded.

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded (teleconsult; no vitals obtained).
- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated:  Not recorded.
- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant:  Not recorded.
- Ear exam including otoscopy:  Not recorded.
- Eye exam: visual acuity, pupil response, fundus if indicated:  Not recorded.
- Urinalysis: dipstick for protein, glucose, ketones, blood:  Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Blood tests: fasting glucose and lipids preferred; HbA1c if diabetes present/suspected:  Not recorded.
- Renal function and liver function tests if clinically indicated:  Not recorded.
- ECG if cardiac risk factors present or baseline:  Not recorded.
- Cervical screening if eligible and due:  Not recorded.
- Mammography if eligible and not up to date:  Not recorded.
- Faecal occult blood test if due:  Not recorded.
- Bone density (DEXA) if osteoporosis risk present:  Not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary of key findings:  Acute onset sore throat progressing to dry cough over 1 week with transient fever, variable course, exertional dyspnea, subjective wheeze, intermittent chest discomfort, and reduced appetite without weight loss. Non-smoker, no prior asthma, peanut allergy, mother with lung cancer. No hemoptysis. Teleconsultation without exam/vitals; patient reports no palpable neck lumps. Sick note provided. Advice given: rest, fluids, paracetamol, and safety-net to seek in-person care if worsening or not improving in 4–5 days.
- Relevant differentials (consistent with DDx and transcript):
  - Acute viral upper respiratory infection with acute bronchitis, including consideration of COVID-19/influenza.
  - Post-viral reactive airway disease/new-onset asthma triggered by infection.
  - Atypical/early community-acquired pneumonia (less likely).
- Working diagnosis:  Acute viral upper respiratory infection with acute bronchitis (high likelihood given sore throat → dry cough sequence, initial fever now resolved, exertional dyspnea/wheeze commonly seen with viral bronchitis, absence of red-flag features).
- Considerations:  
  - Post-viral reactive airway disease/new-onset asthma (medium likelihood; dry cough, subjective wheeze, exertional SOB after URI; no prior history).  
  - Atypical/community-acquired pneumonia (low–medium; initial fever and chest discomfort but currently afebrile, non-productive cough, mild symptoms).  
  - Pulmonary embolism (low; lacks risk factors; symptoms align with viral illness).  
  - Chest wall strain/costochondritis from coughing (low; may explain chest discomfort only).
- Conflicts noted:  
  - Date of birth recorded as 09-May-2016 conflicts with adult employment and context.  
  - Chest pain history inconsistent: patient affirmed chest pain earlier but later clinician restated “you say you don't have any chest pain”; discrepancy unresolved.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Advised rest, adequate fluids, and paracetamol for symptom relief; safety-net to seek in-person assessment if worsening or not improving in 4–5 days or if breathlessness acutely worsens.
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Not recorded.
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not recorded.
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  Not recorded.
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  Advised to see a GP in person if symptoms worsen or fail to improve within 4–5 days.

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral:  Not recorded.
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  Not recorded.
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  Not recorded.
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  Not recorded.
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  Not recorded.
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Acute viral URI with acute bronchitis (including COVID-19/influenza) – High likelihood: Classic progression from sore throat to dry cough with brief fever and subsequent partial improvement; mild exertional SOB/wheeze can accompany viral bronchitis; no red flags.
- Post-viral reactive airway disease/new-onset asthma – Medium likelihood: Viral illness followed by dry cough, subjective wheeze, and exertional dyspnea; atopic history (peanut allergy) may increase propensity; no prior asthma history.
- Atypical/community-acquired pneumonia – Low–Medium likelihood: Initial fever, cough, and chest discomfort could represent early/atypical pneumonia, but current afebrile state and mild symptoms argue against established pneumonia.

Quality checks

- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vitals (BP, pulse, temperature, SpO2), BMI/anthropometrics, respiratory exam, immunization review (influenza/COVID-19/pneumococcal/shingles/tetanus), chronic disease screening (glucose/lipids, CRC screening, bone density where indicated), smoking/alcohol/AOD quantification, mental health screening, hearing/vision screening, urinalysis.
- Internal conflicts or contradictions: DOB suggests a child, while social context indicates an employed adult (conflict noted). Chest pain history inconsistent between patient report and later summary (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality notes: Telehealth visit without physical exam or vitals; some unclear or interrupted responses; consultation ended abruptly due to time constraints.
